claim: British media baron Robert Maxwell — Ghislaine Maxwell's father and the subject of long-standing Mossad-tie allegations — completed a roughly $2.5–2.6 billion hostile takeover of Macmillan Inc., the American publishing house, on November 4, 1988. It was the first hostile takeover of a U.S. publisher, and Macmillan was a major educational and reference publisher. Maxwell's media empire collapsed amid revelations of massive pension-fund fraud after his death at sea in November 1991. A further claim — that Maxwell 'used it to control the contents of the textbooks distributed to American school children' to 'rewrite our past' — is unsupported: ownership of an education publisher is documented; editorial direction of textbook content by Maxwell is not.
